work_order.understanding: Reproduced on the versions this repo actually ships: cmdk 1.1.1 with @radix-ui/react-dialog 1.1.15 (yarn.lock:6684). Every open of the command palette logs two console messages from Radix: the error '`DialogContent` requires a `DialogTitle` for the component to be accessible for screen reader users.' and the warning 'Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.' The dialog also renders aria-labelledby="radix-_r_1_" pointing at an element that does not exist, so the palette has no real accessible name despite the props it already passes. THE ISSUE'S STATED CAUSE IS WRONG, and this matters because it is what points at the forbidden fix. The body claims that because the warning fires while CommandBar.tsx passes aria-label, 'that label is evidently not reaching the underlying DialogContent', and that 'Radix suppresses the warning when DialogContent receives aria-label={undefined}'. Both halves are false. cmdk's Command.Dialog (dist/index.js, xe) destructures only {open, onOpenChange, overlayClassName, contentClassName, container, ...p} and renders Dialog.Content with exactly three props: aria-label={e.label}, cmdk-dialog, className — so DialogContent's accessible name comes from the label prop, which CommandBar.tsx:273 already passes as t('Command Bar'); the label is already reaching it. Radix 1.1.15's TitleWarning consults only document.getElementById(context.titleId) and never reads aria-label at all. And removing both props changes nothing: with label and aria-label stripped, aria-label comes back null and BOTH warnings still fire. So the fix is not about where a label goes, and the route the issue text implies — passing or removing an aria-label — is a dead end. The real defect is that cmdk never renders DialogTitle or DialogDescription. It is fixed by rendering both as visually-hidden children of Command.Dialog, verified to drop the captured console output to zero while both aria-labelledby and aria-describedby resolve to real elements. The second warning is not mentioned in the ticket but fires on the same open from the same cause and is in scope: the body asks for the palette to open silently, and a Title-only fix still leaves a warning in the console. That is the one scope judgment here and it is called out so a maintainer can reject it. Removing the accessible name is not an option — it is explicitly forbidden by the ticket and, per the disproof above, it would not even silence the warning.
work_order.root_cause: cmdk 1.1.1's Command.Dialog renders Dialog.Content with an aria-label but never renders a DialogTitle or DialogDescription, so no element ever carries the id that Radix's context hands to Dialog.Content as aria-labelledby. Radix 1.1.15 unconditionally sets aria-labelledby={titleId} (useId, always truthy) and warns when document.getElementById(titleId) is null, so the warning fires on every open regardless of any aria-label. The fix is to render a DialogTitle and DialogDescription; cmdk spreads children onto the inner Command root, which sits inside Dialog.Content, and Radix's check is a document-wide getElementById, so both land in the live tree. Title alone is not enough — verified: Title-without-Description still leaves one captured warning.

Adding @radix-ui/react-dialog as a direct dependency with the same ^1.1.6 range cmdk uses should dedupe to the existing 1.1.15. review.title: The assertion the test is named for — that opening the palette logs no dialog accessibility warning — can pass on unfixed code, because it reads `messages` before Playwright has delivered the console events Radix emits. The Radix warnings fire from a `useEffect` inside the freshly-mounted dialog, and `page.on('console')` delivers them asynchronously over CDP; the only await between the keypress and the assertion is `expect(...).toBeVisible()`, which resolves as soon as the combobox is painted, not when console traffic has drained. On unfixed code the array can therefore still be empty when compared, the assertion passes, and the test only fails later on the aria assertions — so the specific regression AC-4 names is not what makes the test red.
review.detail:
The assertion the test is named for — that opening the palette logs no dialog accessibility warning — can pass on unfixed code, because it reads `messages` before Playwright has delivered the console events Radix emits. The Radix warnings fire from a `useEffect` inside the freshly-mounted dialog, and `page.on('console')` delivers them asynchronously over CDP; the only await between the keypress and the assertion is `expect(...).toBeVisible()`, which resolves as soon as the combobox is painted, not when console traffic has drained. On unfixed code the array can therefore still be empty when compared, the assertion passes, and the test only fails later on the aria assertions — so the specific regression AC-4 names is not what makes the test red.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:62`

Evidence: Order in the added test is: `await page.keyboard.press('ControlOrMeta+k')` -> `await expect(page.getByRole('combobox', {name: 'Command Bar'})).toBeVisible()` -> `expect(messages).toEqual([])`. Nothing awaits a console event or event-loop turn between statements 2 and 3. In the jsdom harness rendering the same component tree, both Radix messages are emitted from a passive effect (TitleWarning -> console.error, DescriptionWarning -> console.warn), not during the commit that makes the combobox visible: `--- withTitle=false --- messages: ["error: \`DialogContent\` requires a \`DialogTitle\`...", "warning: Warning: Missing \`Description\` or \`aria-describedby={undefined}\`..."] aria-labelledby= radix-_r_1_ -> null; aria-describedby= radix-_r_2_ -> null`. The test's own comment asserts the opposite rationale — "Assert the console first: it is the regression this test exists for, and the failure below would otherwise mask it" — which is inverted: asserting first is only correct if the value is already complete, and this is the value most likely to be incomplete.

Fix: Give the console listener a deterministic drain point before asserting. Simplest correct form: move the console assertion to the end of the test, after the aria assertions have awaited, plus an explicit settle such as `await expect(dialog).toBeVisible()`. Or gate the comparison on a Promise resolved by the console handler. Since the aria-describedby/aria-labelledby assertions are synchronous DOM state already awaited via `referredText`, they can carry the regression on their own with the console check kept as a secondary assertion at the end.

review.title: The regex is materially broader than its own comment claims, and two of its five alternatives match generic attribute names that appear in ordinary application output, not just in Radix's two warnings. Any console error or warning anywhere in the app mentioning `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` fails this test even when the dialog is fine. The comment says "Matched narrowly so the test fails on these two warnings without flaking on unrelated app noise", which is not what the pattern does.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:12`

Evidence: `grep -rn "aria-labelledby\|aria-describedby" packages/desktop-client/src/` returns nothing today, so there is no current false positive — which is exactly why the breadth is a latent flake rather than a present break. But the harness run on the real component tree shows the app's console is not silent in general: rendering `Command.Dialog` also produced `error: Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop` from cmdk's own rendering. Any future log line naming those attributes flips this test red for a reason unrelated to the palette.

Fix: Anchor the pattern to Radix's actual message text rather than to attribute names: /DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle|Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby/. If the attribute-name alternatives are kept as defence in depth, correct the comment to say they are intentionally broad.

review.title: `expect(await referredText(dialog, 'aria-describedby')).toBe('Search pages, accounts and reports')` hard-codes an English literal, and the new string has no translation yet. It passes today only because Playwright forces `availableLanguages` to `[]` and i18next's `fallbackLng: false` makes the natural-language key render as itself. It is brittle against any change that lets a locale load under test, and it pins exact copy rather than the relationship the fix establishes.

It passes today only because Playwright forces `availableLanguages` to `[]` and i18next's `fallbackLng: false` makes the natural-language key render as itself. `packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:78`

Evidence: packages/desktop-client/src/i18n.ts:9 `export const availableLanguages = Platform.isPlaywright ? [] : ...` and i18n.ts:32 `fallbackLng: false` with `nsSeparator: false, keySeparator: false` — i18next returns the key verbatim for an untranslated string, so under Playwright Trans renders 'Search pages, accounts and reports'. A locale sync landing before this test ever runs in a non-English configuration would break it.

Fix: Assert the relationship rather than the copy: expect aria-describedby to resolve to a non-empty element (toBeTruthy()), keeping the exact-text assertion only for the title, whose English string is already covered by the pre-existing `getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Command Bar' })`.

Evidence: `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:120` defines `Maintenance` as "Internal changes that don't directly affect users" and `Bugfix` as "Bug fixes". `grep -h '^category:' upcoming-release-notes/*.md | sort | uniq -c` gives: 29 Bugfix, 22 Enhancements, 18 Maintenance, 7 Features, 6 Bugfixes, 1 Enhancement. The work order prescribed `Maintenance`, so this is the work order's choice carried out faithfully rather than implementer drift — raised here so a maintainer can settle it rather than have it settle itself at release time.

Fix: Change `category: Maintenance` to `category: Bugfix` in upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-title-warning.md, and correct the same line in the work order so the next run does not reintroduce it. If `Maintenance` is deliberate — treating a silenced dev-console warning as internal — leave it and say so; either is defensible, but it should be a decision rather than a default.

review.title: The new `referredText` helper types its locator as `ReturnType<Page['locator']>` and casts inside it with `attr as string`. Both drift from the surrounding file and from AGENTS.md. Every other e2e file in the repo — 32 of them, including `fixtures.ts:2` in this same directory — imports `Locator` by name from `@playwright/test`; `grep -rn 'ReturnType' packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns nothing else, so this is the only indirect spelling in the suite. And the cast is dead weight: `attribute` is already typed `'aria-labelledby' | 'aria-describedby'`, which is assignable to `string`, so `as string` narrows nothing — while AGENTS.md states plainly "Prefer `satisfies` over type assertions (`as`, `!`)".
